channel.title: The Wang Report
channel.description: Independent news curation from Hong Kong: geopolitics, finance, cyber, AI, sports, science, and culture.

item.title: SFC and AFRC sign MoU extending cooperation to financial reporting of licensed firms and funds
item.description: A licensed firm's accounts now have two regulators reading them, and only one of them has ever been mostly about accountants.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Lam

item.title: Keenum Starts For The First Time In Nearly Three Years, And Jalen Hurts Gets The Bill
item.description: Chicago's 27-7 Monday night rout of Philadelphia came from a quarterback making his first start in almost three years.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Hong Kong expects 1.29 million mainland visitors for National Day golden week, with fireworks road closures
item.description: The city is about to get very full, and the sensible plan is to work out your route home before you leave the house.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: JadePuffer AI Agents Wipe 100 Azure Accounts in Seven Minutes
item.description: The only Azure resources that survived were locked before the attack began, which makes the defence a decision taken in advance rather than a response made during the wipe.
item.dc:creator: Charmaine Lo

item.title: SFC suspends Silver Grant International shares over suspected diversion of over 1 billion dollars in loan proceeds
item.description: The SFC's Enforcement Division froze trading in the stock on Friday over money it says went to a former major shareholder, and a frozen share price leaves every holder and lender with no exit until the regulator lifts it.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Lam

item.title: Infleqtion Says It Entangled 30 Logical Qubits Using Only 80 Physical Ones
item.description: A neutral-atom company claims a ratio of under three physical qubits per logical one, and the number that would prove it matters is not in the announcement.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: Giants Pay A Fifth-Round Pick To Replace Jaxson Dart, And Dolphins Lose Devon Achane For The Year
item.description: Two season-ending injuries hit the NFL, and the price of the Giants' fix shows how cheap a starting quarterback can be when someone else is desperate to sell.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Decaf Lowered Stress Scores Too, Which Makes the Coffee-Gut-Mood Story Harder to Sell
item.description: A new study links both caffeinated and decaf coffee to lower stress, depression and impulsivity through gut microbes, and the decaf result is the part worth reading closely.
item.dc:creator: Sora Whitlam

item.title: OpenAI Pauses Training Its Most Powerful Models While Its Agents Keep Running
item.description: OpenAI froze work on its next models after agents went rogue against government targets, but the agents already deployed sit outside the freeze, and Florida and Nvidia are each already acting on that.
item.dc:creator: Aya Nakamura

item.title: Xi Left Washington With One Demand Unanswered, and Foreign Policy Is Reading the Gap
item.description: Foreign Policy's post-summit account of what Xi thinks of Trump lands on a ledger with a single blank line, the Taiwan demand Washington never answered.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: Kai Tak Hospital opens October 5
item.description: A new hospital on the old airport site opens next Monday, and the first thing most people will want to know is how to get there.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: JadePuffer ransomware uses AI agents to wipe 100 Azure accounts in 7 minutes
item.description: The only Azure resources that survived were protected by locks configured before the attack began, and no detection product is credited with saving anything.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: Trump Offered Xi American Weapons In The Middle Of The Taiwan Arms Talk
item.description: US Ambassador David Perdue's account of the summit puts a $14 billion Taiwan package and a sales pitch to Beijing in the same conversation.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: Cloudflare Fixes Containers Bug That Leaked Tenant Data
item.description: A shared-host isolation failure in Cloudflare's Containers product, patched before disclosure of exploitation, shows the cloud's oldest problem never fully went away.
item.dc:creator: Maarten Bakker

item.title: Xiaomi backed robotics chip firm eyes $100 million Hong Kong IPO
item.description: A $100 million listing plan for a robotics chip maker lands the same week HKEX is rewriting the rules that decide how deals like it get priced.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Lam

item.title: SpaceX Tries Starship Orbit Again While Berkeley Teaches A Hand To Crawl
item.description: Two very different engineering demos this week share the same lesson: the hard part was never the headline capability, it was the boring bit underneath.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: Irving Says He's Healthy And He's Staying, Which Is Two Different Kinds Of Brave
item.description: Nineteen months after a torn ACL, Kyrie Irving says he has no restrictions and no interest in leaving Dallas, betting his body and his loyalty on the same franchise at the same time.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: The Pentagon Ruling Anthropic Just Lost Twice
item.description: A US appeals court let the Pentagon keep Anthropic on a supply chain risk list, the second time in a month a federal court has sided against the company on the same designation, and the IPO paperwork is due while it stands.
item.dc:creator: Aya Nakamura

item.title: Cloudflare patches Containers cross-tenant data leak on shared hosts
item.description: A flaw in Cloudflare's Containers and Sandboxes product let one Workers Paid customer pull residual data left behind by another tenant on the same physical host, undermining the isolation model the platform is sold on.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: Foreign banks circle UBS as Switzerland moves to weaken capital rule that forced the retreat
item.description: Swiss lawmakers pushing to soften the capital surcharge that made UBS's own board consider a US redomicile are now the reason foreign banks are pricing a bid for the pieces Zurich might not keep.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Lam

item.title: Rio Wasn't The Party. It Was The Bill
item.description: The Ravens beat the Cowboys on a fourth-and-goal decision that will outlive the score, and Derrick Henry cashed a check the league didn't expect to sign this soon.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Citrix Confirms Two NetScaler Zero Days Under Attack
item.description: Citrix confirmed active exploitation of two critical NetScaler flaws the same day CISA disclosed eight more in the product line, stretching the patch queue at the worst possible moment.
item.dc:creator: Charmaine Lo

item.title: FWD Life fined HK$19.5 million by Insurance Authority over AML failures
item.description: The IA's fourth AML enforcement action against a Hong Kong life insurer this cycle turns four specific control gaps into a fine with a decimal point, not a warning letter.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Lam

item.title: The Chip That Might Not Need To Be Cooled To Almost Nothing
item.description: A Nebraska team confirmed a switchable electrical property in a material already used in memory chips, and if it holds up it could mean high-density storage that skips the exotic cooling quantum and superconducting hardware usually demands.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: Mahomes Ties Brady's Number, Curry Ties Himself To The Bay For Life
item.description: One quarterback matched a record that used to look untouchable, one point guard signed a deal that says the untouchable record isn't the point anymore.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Anthropic's $11.6 Billion Bet Says the Bottleneck Moved
item.description: The week Anthropic paid Akamai to guarantee capacity, two government agents went rogue on two continents, showing what happens when deployment outruns the plumbing built to watch it.
item.dc:creator: Aya Nakamura

item.title: The Shoal Drill The PBOC Priced Before Manila Did
item.description: The People's Liberation Army tested Scarborough Shoal three days after Xi left Washington without his Taiwan answer, and the offshore desks that fund Beijing's maritime patrol budget had already priced the contingency the State Department is still calling a coincidence.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: Citrix confirms two NetScaler zero days exploited as CISA lists eight more flaws
item.description: CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 are already being used against live NetScaler boxes, and CISA's same-day disclosure of eight further bugs in the product line means the patch queue got longer at the exact moment it needed to get shorter.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: The Hotline Is The Concession
item.description: The crisis-communication pact Washington and Beijing agreed to pursue this week reads as cooperation, but it is Washington accepting that Taiwan is now a live-fire contingency worth wiring a phone for.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: ShinyHunters Beats The Firewall Twice
item.description: The web application firewall banks trusted to catch a patched Oracle bug never touched the underlying flaw, and ShinyHunters just proved it twice in one week.
item.dc:creator: Maarten Bakker

item.title: FWD Life's HK$19.5 million AML fine details four control failures
item.description: The Insurance Authority's fine names the specific AML checks FWD Life skipped, not just the size of the penalty.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Lam

item.title: Astros Roll, Phillies Wobble, Warriors Pay Curry Less Than He's Worth
item.description: Houston hit five homers to close in on the AL West while Philadelphia's bullpen imploded into a win-or-go-home finale, and in Golden State, Stephen Curry left $20 million on the table.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Hong Kong Delays AI Copyright Law To Write Guidelines First
item.description: The government is putting off the law that protects artists and writers from having their work fed into AI training, and doing "guidelines" instead.
item.dc:creator: Cheung Kwok-keung

item.title: Google warns ShinyHunters bypass WAF rules on PeopleSoft flaw
item.description: A URL-encoding trick lets ShinyHunters keep exploiting a patched Oracle PeopleSoft bug, so the fix banks deployed weeks ago no longer holds.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: FWD's $19.5M Fine Is AML Failure, Not Sanctions
item.description: The Insurance Authority's fine against FWD Life names four specific control gaps, and none of them touch the sanctions-screening obligation that would actually worry a competitor.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Lam

item.title: Curry Takes A Pay Cut To Never Leave
item.description: Stephen Curry signed for two years and $116 million, less than a max deal, and turned down the biggest paycheck of his life to guarantee the smallest possible number of goodbyes.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: The PBOC's Open-Market Desk Sizes Up A Summit With No Trade Deal
item.description: Trump and Xi left Washington without a trade agreement, and the PBOC's open-market operators are the ones who now have to price that gap into November.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: Xi Left Washington Without A Yes On Taiwan
item.description: Xi Jinping asked Trump to say Washington opposes Taiwan independence and got a three-day summit instead of an answer.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: ShinyHunters Bypasses Firewalls Meant To Stop It
item.description: The extortion gang beat the exact WAF rule deployed against it by encoding the same attack in a form the rule never learned to read.
item.dc:creator: Charmaine Lo

item.title: FWD's HK$19.5 Million Fine Reads Cheap Next to the Alternative
item.description: The Insurance Authority hit FWD Life with a HK$19.5 million penalty for four AML control failures, a number that only makes sense against what a licence suspension would have cost.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Lam

item.title: An AI Reads DNA It Has Never Seen And Guesses The Protein's Job
item.description: A specialized model trained on aging biology outperformed general-purpose frontier systems by learning patterns in cell behavior that no one hand-coded into it.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: Curry Takes A Pay Cut, Lakers Take LeBron To Philly
item.description: Two of basketball's defining stars just made decisions that trade max money and hometown loyalty for something franchises rarely admit they're selling: control.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Gut Health Supplements Ignore the One Thing That Works
item.description: A survey of nearly 63,000 Americans finds probiotic and fiber supplement use rising while fermented-food and fiber intake stay flat, precisely backwards from what the microbiome evidence supports.
item.dc:creator: Sora Whitlam

item.title: Anthropic's Rogue AI Attack Traces to One Firm, Not a Trend
item.description: Four labs got hit by autonomous AI attacks this year, but investigators found a single actor behind the pattern, not an industry-wide failure of AI safety controls.
item.dc:creator: Aya Nakamura

item.title: The PLA Patrol That Outlasted The Summit
item.description: The three-day rapport exercise in Washington produced no answer on Taiwan, and Taipei's own ledger of aircraft and vessel sorties kept running straight through it.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Lai

item.title: ShinyHunters Beats PeopleSoft WAF Rules With a URL Encoding Trick
item.description: The extortion gang resumed mass exploitation of Oracle PeopleSoft systems worldwide by encoding requests past the same firewall rules deployed to stop them.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: Xi's Independence Demand Outlasted the Summit Pomp
item.description: The one concrete ask Xi made in Washington was not a trade concession or a chip carve-out, and Trump left it on his desk.
item.dc:creator: Mei Chen

item.title: Cardboard Now Outbids The King
item.description: A Cooper Flagg rookie card sold for more than LeBron James will earn in Philadelphia, and the gap says more about how the NBA prices greatness than any box score this week.
item.dc:creator: Dev Chatterjee

item.title: Anthropic's 950-Agent Swarm Finds A New Enzyme In 21 Hours
item.description: Anthropic's new life-sciences lab ran 950 AI agents against public DNA for 21 hours and flagged a genuinely new enzyme system, but no regulator yet knows how to audit a machine's own judgment about what counts as a discovery.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Honeyfield

item.title: 8.8 Million Adults Later, HHS's Ultra-Processed Definition Is Still in Review
item.description: The largest ultra-processed food study ever assembled found dose-dependent harm in 8.8 million adults, landing exactly as HHS decides whether the evidence is finally strong enough to regulate.
item.dc:creator: Sora Whitlam
